units.sanskrit: दुःखत्रयाभिघाताज्जिज्ञासा तदभिघातके हेतौ ।
units.english: On account of affliction from threefold misery, inquiry should be instituted into the means for its removal.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टे सापार्था चेन्नैकान्तात्यन्ततो ऽभावात् ॥
units.english: If it be said that it is useless because of the existence of evident means then we reply no, because of the absence of certainty and finality.

units.sanskrit: दुःखत्रयेति । अस्या आर्य्याया उपोद्घातः क्रियते । इह भगवान्ब्रह्मसुतः कपिलो नाम ।
units.english: The threefold misery, etc. This āryā is introducedThe exalted sage, Kapila by name, was the son of Brahman.

units.sanskrit: सनकश्च सनन्दश्च तृतीयश्च सनातनः । आसुरिः कपिलश्चैव वोढुः पञ्चशिखस्तथा । इत्येते ब्रह्मणः पुत्राः सप्त प्रोक्ता महर्षयः ॥
units.english: As it is said “Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana the third, Āsuri, Kapila, Vodhu and Pañcaśikha, these seven sages are said to be the sons of Brahman.” Virtue, knowledge, renunciation and power were born with Kapila.

units.sanskrit: एवं स उत्पन्नः सन्नन्धतमसि मज्जज्जगदालोक्य संसारपारम्पर्य्येण सत्कारुण्यो जिज्ञासमानाय आसुरिसगोत्राय ब्रह्मणायेदं पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानां ज्ञानमुक्तवान् ।
units.english: Thus born, seeing this world sinking in the blinding gloom and the succession of samsāra birth and death, he became filled with compassion and taught this knowledge of twentyfive principles to the brahmin Āsuri, born in his own family,the knowledge by which misery comes to an end.

units.sanskrit: यस्य ज्ञानाद्दुःखक्षयो भवति । पञ्चविंशतितत्वज्ञो यत्र तत्राश्रमे वसेत् । जटी मुण्डी शिखी वापि मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
units.english: “One endowed with the knowledge of the twentyfive principles will undoubtedly get salvation, no matter in what stage of life he is, whether he has matted hair, or is shaved or has topknot.” So it is saidOn account of affliction from threefold misery inquiry should be instituted.

units.sanskrit: दुःखत्रयाभिघाताज्जिज्ञासेति ।
units.english: The three kinds of misery are, internal, external and divine.

units.sanskrit: तत्राध्यात्मिकं द्विविधं शारीरं मानसं चेति ।
units.english: The internal twofold bodily and mental.

units.sanskrit: शारीरं वातपित्तश्लेष्मविपर्य्ययकृतं ज्वरातीसारादि । मानसं प्रियवियोगाप्रियसंयोगादि ।
units.english: The bodily misery,fever, dysentry and the rest,is due to the disorder of wind, bile or phlegm mental is separation from what is liked, and union with what is not liked and the rest.

units.sanskrit: आधिभौतिकं चतुर्विधं भूतग्रामनिमित्तं मनुष्यपशुमृगपक्षिसरीसृपदंशमशकयूकामत्कुणमत्स्यमकरग्राहस्थावरेभ्यो जरायुजाण्डजस्वेदजोद्भिज्जेभ्यः सकाशादुपजायते ।
units.english: The external misery, due to fourfold living beings, vis., viviparous, oviparous, born of sweat and born of soil, arises from men, beasts, deer, birds, serpents, gnats, mosquitos, lice, bugs, alligators, sharks, unmoving objects and the rest.

units.sanskrit: आधिदैविकं देवानामिदं दैविकम् । दिवः प्रभवतीति वा दैवं तदधिकृत्य यदुपजायते शीतोष्णवातवर्षाशनिपातादिकम् ।
units.english: The divine misery,i.e., daiva, because it belongs to gods or comes from heaven, that which arises with reference to these,is cold, heat, storm, rain, thunderbolt, and the rest.

units.sanskrit: एवं यथा दुःखत्रयाभिज्ञाताज्जिज्ञासा कार्य्या क्व ।
units.english: Thus, on account of affliction from threefold misery, inquiry should be instituted.

units.sanskrit: तदभिघातके हेतौ ।
units.english: Into what? Into the means for its removal.

units.sanskrit: तस्य दुःखत्रयस्य अभिघातको यो ऽसौ हेतुस्तत्रेति ।
units.english: Therein which is the means for this removal of that threefold misery.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टे सापार्था चेत् । दृष्टे हेतौ दुःखत्रयाभिघातके सा जिज्ञासापार्था चेद्यदि ।
units.english: If it be said that it is useless because of the existence of evident means if it be said that when the evident means for removing the threefold misery are known, this inquiry is useless.

units.sanskrit: तत्राध्यात्मिकस्य द्विविधस्यापि आयुर्वेदशास्त्रक्रियया प्रियसमागमाप्रियपरिहारकटुतिक्तकषायादिक्वाथादिभिर्दृष्ट एव आध्यात्मिकोपायः ।
units.english: For removing the twofold internal misery, the internal means in the shape of treatment according to medical science, union with the liked ones, preclusion of undesirable, the pungent, bitter and astringent decoctions and the like, are quite evident.

units.sanskrit: आधिभौतिकस्य रक्षादिनाभिघातो दृष्टः ।
units.english: In the case of affliction from external misery, the evident means for its removal are seen in the shape of protection and the like.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टे सापार्था चेदेवं मन्यसे । न ।
units.english: If you think that it i.e. inquiry is useless in the presence of evident means, then we reply, no.

units.sanskrit: एकान्त्यात्यन्ततो ऽभावात् ।
units.english: Because of the absence of certainty and finality.

units.sanskrit: यत एकान्ततो ऽवश्यं अत्यन्ततो नित्यं दृष्टेन हेतुनाभिघातो न भवति तस्मादन्यत्र एकान्तात्यन्ताभिघातके हेतौ जिज्ञासा विविदिषा कार्येति ॥
units.english: Because the evident means do not certainly ekāntataḥ and finally atyantataḥ remove it. Therefore, inquiry should be elsewhere instituted into finding out the means which certainly and finally remove the misery.

units.sanskrit: यदि दृष्टान्यत्र जिज्ञासा कार्य्या ततो ऽपि नैव यत आनुश्रविको हेतुर्दुःखत्रयाभिघातकः ।
units.english: If inquiry is to be instituted into other than the evident means, still no. Because the revealed means are known to remove the threefold misery.

units.sanskrit: अनुश्रवतीत्यनुश्रवस्तत्रभवः आनुश्रविकः स च आगमात्सिद्धः ।
units.english: Anuśrava is that which is revealed the means arising from it are called ānuśravika.

units.sanskrit: यथा अपाम सोमममृता अभूमागन्म ज्योतिरविदाम देवान् ।
units.english: That is proved by the Veda as it is said “We have drunk Soma, become immortal, reached the Heaven and become acquainted with gods.

units.sanskrit: किन्नूनमस्मान् कृणवदरातिः किमु धूर्त्तिरमृतमर्त्यस्य ॥ कदाचिदिन्द्रादीनां देवानां कल्प आसीत् ।
units.english: Therefore, indeed, O Immortal One, what can an enemy do against us, how can the old age of a mortal affect us.” Once upon a time there was a discussion among the gods, viz., Indra and others How did we become immortal?

units.sanskrit: कथं वयममृता अभूमेति विचार्य्यामुं यस्माद्वयमपाम सोमं पीतवन्तः सोमं तस्मादमृता अभूम अमरा भूतवन्त इत्यर्थः किंच अगन्म ज्योतिः गतवतो लब्धवतो ज्योतिः स्वर्गमिति ।
units.english: Having pondered, they concludedBecause weapāma somamhave drunk soma, we have become immortal. Moreover, aganma jyotiḥ,we have gone, i.e., achieved jyotis, i.e., Heaven.

units.sanskrit: अविदाम देवान् दिव्यान् विदितवन्तः ।
units.english: Avidāma devān,we have become acquainted with the divine beings.

units.sanskrit: एवं च किन्नूनमस्मान् कृणवदरातिः नूनं निश्चितं किं अरातिः शत्रुरस्मान् कृणवत् कर्त्तेति किमु धूर्त्तिरमृतमर्त्यस्य धूर्त्तिर्जरा हिंसा वा किं करिष्यति अमृतमर्त्यस्य ।
units.english: And so,kim nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ nūnam, i.e., certainly, what can arāti, i.e., enemy, kṛṇavad, i.e., do to us? kima dhūrtir amṭta martyasya O Immortal One he amṛta, what can dhūrtiḥ, i.e., old age or injury of mortal martyasya do to us?

units.sanskrit: अन्यच्च श्रूयते आत्यन्तिकं फलं पशुवधेन । सर्व्वंल्लोकाञ्जयति मृत्युं तरति पाप्मानं तरति ब्रह्महत्यां तरति यो यो ऽश्वमेधेन यजत इति । एकान्तात्यन्तिके एव वेदोक्ते अपार्थे ऽवजिज्ञासा इति न ।
units.english: Moreover, it is said in the Vedas that final goal is achieved by killing animals in sacrifice “He who performs the aśvamedha sacrifice conquers all the regions, transgresses death, transgresses sin, and also transgresses the sin arising from the murder of a brahmin.” Thus, when certain and final means are revealed in the Vedas, the inquiry is useless,No.

units.sanskrit: उच्यते । दृष्टवदानुश्रविकः स ह्यविशुद्धिक्षयातिशययुक्तः ।
units.english: It is said The revealed is like the evident one, It is linked with impurity, destruction and inequality.

units.sanskrit: तद्विपरीतः श्रेयान् व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञविज्ञानात् ॥
units.english: Other than that is better,proceeding from the right cognition of the Manifest, Unmanifest and the Knower.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टवदानुश्रविक इति दृष्टेन तुल्यो दृष्टवत् ।
units.english: The revealed is like the evident one dṛṣṭavat, i.e., like the evident, namely, that what is revealed.

units.sanskrit: को ऽसौ आनुश्रविकः कस्मात्स यस्मादविशुद्धिक्षयातिशययुक्तः । अविशुद्धियुक्तः पशुघातात् तथा चोक्तम् ।
units.english: Why is it like the evident one? Because Linked with impurity, destruction and inequality Linked with impurity, because of the slaughter of animals.

units.sanskrit: षट् शतानि नियुज्यन्ते पशुनां मध्यमे ऽहनि । अश्वमेधस्य वचनादूनानि पशुहिस्त्रिभिः ॥ यद्यपि श्रुतिस्मृतिविहितो धर्म्मस्तथापि मिश्रीभावादविशुद्धियुक्त इति । यथा
units.english: As it is said “According to the injunction in the aśvamedha, six hundred animals, minus three, are employed i.e., slaughtered at midday.” Although, dharma is prescribed by the Śrutis and the Smṛtis, still, on account of the mixture of items, it is full of impurity.

units.sanskrit: बहूनीन्द्रसहस्राणि देवानां च युगे युगे ।
units.english: Again, “In every yuga thousands of Indras and gods have been surpassed by the time.

units.sanskrit: कालेन समतीतानि कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः ॥ एवमिन्द्रादिनाशात्क्षययुक्तः ।
units.english: Time is therefore unsurpassable.” Thus, it is linked with destruction, on account of the destruction of Indra and others.

units.sanskrit: तथातिशयो विशेषस्तेन युक्तः ।
units.english: Again, it is endowed with atiśaya, i.e., inequality due to superiority.

units.sanskrit: विशेषगुणादर्शनादितरस्य दुःखं स्यादिति ।
units.english: By seeing superiority in one, the other feels pain.

units.sanskrit: एवमानुश्रविको ऽपि हेतुर्दृष्टवत् ।
units.english: Thus the revealed means are like the evident ones.

units.sanskrit: कस्तर्हि श्रेयानिति चेत् । उच्यते । तद्विपरीतः श्रेयान् ताभ्यां दृष्टानुश्रविकाभ्यां विपरीतः श्रेयान् प्रशस्यतर इति ।
units.english: If it be asked which is better, then it is replied Other than that is better Other than the revealed and the evident ones is better.

units.sanskrit: अविशुद्धिक्षयातिशयायुक्तत्वात् ।
units.english: Because, it is free from impurity, destruction and inequality.

units.sanskrit: स कथमित्याह ।
units.english: How is it acquired?

units.sanskrit: व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञविज्ञानात् तत्र व्यक्तं महदादिबुद्धिरहंकारः पञ्च तन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चमहाभूतानि ।
units.english: The author replies, From the right cognition of the Manifest, Unmanifest, and Knower The Manifest are mahat and the rest that is, intellect, ego the five subtle elements, the eleven organs and the five gross elements.

units.sanskrit: अव्यक्तं प्रधानम् ।
units.english: The Unmamfest is the Pradhāna.

units.sanskrit: ज्ञः पुरुषः ।
units.english: The Knower is the Puruṣa.

units.sanskrit: एवमेतानि पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानि व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञानि कथ्यन्ते एतद्विज्ञानाच्छ्रेय इत्युक्तं च पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वज्ञ इति ॥ अथ व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञानां को विशेष इत्युच्यते ।
units.english: Thus, these twentyfive principles are called the Manifest, the Unmanifest and the Knower. In their right cognition lies the preference over the other means. It has also been said“One endowed with the knowledge of the twentyfive principles.” etc. Now, what are the special characteristics of the Manifest, the Unmanifest and the Knower?

units.sanskrit: मूलप्रकृतिरविकृतिर्महदाद्याः प्रकृतिविकृतयः सप्त । षोडशकस्तु विकारो न प्रकृतिर्न विकृतिः पुरुषः ॥
units.english: We reply Primal Nature is not an evolute Mahat, etc., the seven, are evolvents and evolutes the group of sixteen is evolute the Spirit is neither an evolute nor an evolvent.

units.sanskrit: मूलप्रकृतिः प्रधानम् । प्रकृतिविकृतिसप्तकस्य मूलभूतत्वात् । मूलं च सा प्रकृतिश्च मूलप्रकृतिरविकृतिः ।
units.english: Primal Nature, i.e. pradhāna, is so called, because it is the origin of the seven evolvents and the evolutes Primal Nature, because it is the origin and a nonproduct, is an evolvent.

units.sanskrit: अन्यस्मान्नोत्पद्यते तेन प्रकृतिः कस्यचिद्विकारो न भवति ।
units.english: As it is not produced from anything, therefore, Nature cannot be an evolute of anything.

units.sanskrit: महदाद्याः प्रकृतिविकृतयः सप्त ।
units.english: Mahat, etc., the seven are evolvents and evolutes.

units.sanskrit: महाभूतादिति बुद्धिः बुद्ध्याद्याः सप्त बुद्धि अहंकारः पञ्चतन्मात्राणि एतानि सप्तप्रकृतिविकृतयः ।
units.english: Mahat, i.e., intellect. Intellect and the rest are seven, viz., intellect, ego and the five subtle elements. They are seven evolvents and evolutes.

units.sanskrit: प्रधानाद्बुद्धिरुत्पद्यते तेन विकृतिः प्रधानस्य विकार इति सैवाहंकारमुत्पादयति अतः प्रकृतिः ।
units.english: That is, intellect is produced from the Nature, therefore, it is a product of the Nature,an evolute. The same intellect produces ego and is, therefore, an evolvent.

units.sanskrit: अहंकारो ऽपि बुद्धेरुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिः स च पञ्चतन्मात्राण्युत्पादयतीति प्रकृतिः ।
units.english: Ego also, being produced from intellect is an evolute and it is an evolvent as it produces the five subtle elements.

units.sanskrit: तत्र शब्दतन्मात्रमहंकारादुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिस्तस्मादाकाशमुत्पद्यत इति प्रकृतिः ।
units.english: The subtle element of sound, being produced from ego is an evolute and it is an evolvent, as it produces ether.

units.sanskrit: तथा स्पर्शतन्मात्रमहंकारादुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिस्तदेवं वायुमुत्पादयतीति प्रकृतिः ।
units.english: Similarly, the subtle element of touch. being produced from ego, is an evolute and it is an evolvent as it produces wind.

units.sanskrit: गन्धतन्मात्रमहंकारादुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिस्तदेवं पृथिवीमुत्पादयतीति प्रकृतिः । रूपतन्मात्रमहंकारादुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिस्तदेवं तेज उत्पादयतीति प्रकृतिः । रसतन्मात्रमहंकारादुत्पद्यत इति विकृतिस्तदेवं आप उत्पादयतीति प्रकृतिः ।
units.english: The subtle element of smell, being produced from ego is an evolute and it is an evolvent as it produces earth. The subtle element of fire, being produced from ego is an evolute and it is an evolvent as it produces light. The subtle element of taste, being produced from ego, is an evolute and it is an evolvent as it produces water.

units.sanskrit: एवं महदाद्याः सप्त प्रकृतयो विकृतयश्च ।
units.english: Thus, mahat, etc., the seven, are evolvents and evolutes.

units.sanskrit: षोडशकश्च विकारः पञ्चबुद्धीन्द्रियाणि पञ्चकर्म्मेन्द्रियाणि एकादशं मनः पञ्चमहाभूतानि एष षोडशको गणो विकृतिरेव ।
units.english: The group of sixteen is evolute. The five organs of sense, the five organs of action, the eleventh mind and the five gross elements, this group of sixteen is only evolute.

units.sanskrit: विकारो विकृतिः ।
units.english: It is but a product.

units.sanskrit: न प्रकृतिर्न विकृतिः पुरुषः ॥
units.english: The Spirit is neither an evolvent nor an evolute.

units.sanskrit: एवमेषां व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञानां त्रयाणां पदार्थानां कैः कियद्भिः प्रमाणैः केन कस्य वा प्रमाणेन सिद्धिर्भवति ।
units.english: By what and how many means of cognition are these three categories, namely the Manifest, the Unmanifest and the Knower known?Which category by which means of cognition?

units.sanskrit: इह लोके प्रमेयवस्तु प्रमाणेन साध्यते यथा प्रस्थादिभिर्व्रीहयस्तुलया चन्दनादि ।
units.english: In this world, the knowables are proved by means of proof, as rice by the weight seer and sandal by balance.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात् प्रमाणमभिधेयम् ।
units.english: Therefore, the means of cognition should be defined.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टमनुमानमाप्तवचनं च सर्वप्रमाणसिद्धत्वात् । त्रिविधं प्रमाणमिष्टं प्रमेयसिद्धिः प्रमाणाद्धि ॥
units.english: The means of right cognition are recognised to be of three kinds,perception. inference and valid testimony as all the means of right cognition are proven to be included in these three.

units.sanskrit: दृष्टं यथा श्रोत्रं त्वक् चक्षुर्जिह्वा घ्राणमिति पञ्चबुद्धीन्द्रियाणि शब्दस्पर्शरूपरसगन्धा एषां पञ्चानां पञ्चैव विषया यथासंख्यं शब्दं श्रोत्रं त्वक् स्पर्शं चक्षू रूपं जिह्वा रसं घ्राणं गन्धमिति ।
units.english: Verily, a provable is proved by means of right cognition. Perception. The ear, the skin, the eye, the tongue, and the nose are the five organs of sense. Sound, touch, sight, taste and smell are respectively the five objects of these. The ear comprehends sound the skin, touch the tongue, taste the nose, smell.

units.sanskrit: एतद्दृष्टमित्युच्यते प्रमाणम् ।
units.english: This means of right cognition is called perception.

units.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षेणानुमानेन व यो ऽर्थो न गृह्यते स आप्तवचनाद्ग्राह्यः ।
units.english: An object which cannot be apprehended by perception or inference is apprehended by valid testimony.

units.sanskrit: यथेन्द्रोः देवराजः उत्तराः कुरवः स्वर्गे ऽप्सरस इत्यादि ।
units.english: For example, the existence of Indra, the king of gods the northern Kurus the nymphs in the Heaven and so on.

units.sanskrit: प्रत्यक्षानुमानाग्राह्यमथाप्तवचनाद्गृह्यते ।
units.english: That which is not apprehended by perception or inference is apprehended by valid testimony.

units.sanskrit: अपि चोक्तम् ।
units.english: Moreover, it is said “Scripture is valid testimony.

units.sanskrit: आगमो ह्याप्तवचनमाप्तं दोषक्षयाद्विदुः ।
units.english: A person is called valid because he is free from blemishes.

units.sanskrit: क्षीणदोषो ऽनृतं वाक्यं न ब्रूयाद्धेत्वसम्भवात् ॥ स्वकर्म्मण्यभियुक्तो यः सङ्गद्वेषविवर्ज्जितः । पूजितस्तद्विधैर्नित्यमाप्तो ज्ञेयः स तादृशः ॥ एतेषु प्रमाणेषु सर्वप्रमाणानि सिद्धानि भवन्ति ।
units.english: He who is free from blemishes will not tell a lie, because there is no occasion for that.” “He who is engaged in his duties is free from attachment and aversion, and is always respected by persons like himself,such a person is known to be valid.” All the other means of cognition are included in these three.

units.sanskrit: षट् प्रमाणानि जैमिनिः ।
units.english: Jaimini says there are six means of right cognition.

units.sanskrit: अर्थापत्तिः सम्भवः अभावः प्रतिभा ऐतिह्यं उपमानं चेति षट् प्रमाणानि ।
units.english: Well, what are these means of right cognition?Presumption arthāpatti, Probability sambhava, Negation abhāva, Imagination pratibhā, Tradition aitihya and Analogy upamāna,are the six means of right cognition.

units.sanskrit: तत्रार्थापत्तिर्द्विविधा दृष्टा श्रुता च । तत्र दृष्टा । एकस्मिन् पक्षे आत्मभावो गृहीतश्चेदन्यस्मिन्नप्यात्मभावो गृह्यत एव ।
units.english: The Presumption is of two kinds“seen or heard.” “Seen”, e.g., if the existence of soul is admitted in one case then it is admitted in other cases as well.

units.sanskrit: श्रुता यथा । दिवा देवदत्तो न भुङ्क्ते अथ च पीनो दृश्यते अतो ऽवगम्यते रात्रौ भुङ्क्त इति ।
units.english: “Heard”, e.g., Devadatta does not eat during the day, and yet he looks stout. Therefore, it is presumed that he eats at night.

units.sanskrit: सम्भवो यथा । प्रस्थ इत्युक्ते चत्वारः कुडवाः सम्भाव्यन्ते ।
units.english: The Probability, e.g., when one says a prastha, the probability of four kuḍavas in it, is established.

units.sanskrit: प्रागितरेतरात्यन्तसर्वाभावलक्षणः ।
units.english: Negation is of the nature of antecedent, mutual, total and consequent.

units.sanskrit: प्रागभावो यथा देवदत्तः कौमारयौवनादिषु ।
units.english: Antecedent Negation, as of Devadatta in boyhood and youth.

units.sanskrit: इतरेतराभावः पटे घटाभावः ।
units.english: Mutual Negation, as of jar in cloth.

units.sanskrit: अत्यन्ताभावः खरविषाणवन्ध्यासुतखपुष्पवदिति । सर्वाभावः प्रध्वंसाभावो दग्धपटवदिति ।
units.english: Total Negation, as of horns in a man, or the son of a barren woman, or a flower in the sky. Consequent Negation is the negation due to destruction, as of a piece of burnt cloth.

units.sanskrit: यथा शुष्कधान्यदर्शनद्वृष्टेरभावो ऽवगम्यते ।
units.english: As a consequence of seeing dry grain, negation of rains is understood.

units.sanskrit: एवमभावो ऽनेकधा ।
units.english: Thus, Negation is of various kinds.

units.sanskrit: पृथिव्यामासमुद्रायां स प्रदेशो मनोरमः । एवमुक्ते तस्मिन् प्रदेशे शोभनाः गुणाः सन्तीति प्रतिभोत्पद्यते प्रतिभान्वाससंज्ञानमिति ।
units.english: Imagination, as “The country lying to the south of the Vindhyas and the north of the Sahya and extending up to the seas, is lovely” hearing this, imagination arises that there are lovely qualities in that country.

units.sanskrit: ऐतिह्यं यथा ।
units.english: Imagination is a cognition which follows an utterance.

units.sanskrit: ब्रवीति लोको यथात्र वटे यक्षिणी प्रवसतीत्येव ऐतिह्यम् ।
units.english: Tradition,as people say that a yakṣiṇi resides on this bunyan tree this is tradition.

units.sanskrit: गौरिव गवयः समुद्र इव तडागम् ।
units.english: Analogy,as a gavaya is like a cow a tank is like sea.

units.sanskrit: एतानि षट् प्रमाणानि त्रिषु दृष्टादिष्वन्तर्भूतानि ।
units.english: These six means of right cognition are comprehended by Perception and the rest.

units.sanskrit: तत्रानुमाने तावदर्थापत्तिरन्तर्भूता । सम्भवाभावप्रतिभैतिह्योपमाश्चाप्तवचने ।
units.english: The Presumption is comprehended by Inference Probability, Negation, Imagination, Tradition and Analogy are comprehended by Valid Testimony.

units.sanskrit: तस्मात्त्रिष्वेव सर्वप्रमाणसिद्धत्वात् त्रिविधं प्रमाणमिष्टं तदाह तेन त्रिविधेन प्रमाणेन प्रमाणसिद्धिर्भवतीतित वाक्यशेषः ।
units.english: Therefore, all the other means of right cognition being proved to be included in these three, only three kinds of means of right cognition are recognised, means that by these three means of right cognition, other means of right cognition are established.

units.sanskrit: प्रमेयसिद्धिः प्रमाणाद्धि ।
units.english: Because, the provables are proved by means of right cognition.

units.sanskrit: प्रमेयं प्रधानं बुद्धिरहंकारः पञ्चतन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चमहाभूतानि पुरुष इति एतानि पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानि व्यक्ताव्यक्तज्ञान्युच्यन्ते ।
units.english: The things to be proved arePrimal Nature, intellect, ego, the five subtle elements, the eleven organs, the five gross elements and the Spirit. These twentyfive categories are called the Manifest, the Unmanifest and the Knower.

units.sanskrit: तत्र किञ्चित् प्रत्यक्षेण साध्यं किञ्चिदनुमानेन किञ्चिदागमेनेति त्रिविधं प्रमाणमुक्तं ॥
units.english: Out of these, some are to be proved by means of Perception, some by Inference and some by Valid Testimony. These are the three means of right cognition.

units.sanskrit: तस्य किं लक्षणमेतदाह । प्रतिविषयाध्यवसायो दृष्टं त्रिविधमनुमानमाख्यातम् । तल्लिङ्गलिङ्गिपूर्वकमाप्तश्रुतिराप्तवचनं तु ॥
units.english: Now the definitions of each are given Perception is the application of senses to their special objects Inference is said to be of three kinds it is preceded by the knowledge of linga the Middle term and the lingin the Major term.

units.sanskrit: प्रतिविषयेषु श्रोत्रादिनां शब्दादिविषयेषु अध्यवसायो दृष्टं प्रत्यक्षमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Dṛṣṭa or Perception is the application of the sensesear and the rest, to their special objects, viz., sound and the rest.

units.sanskrit: त्रिविधमनुमानमाख्यातं शेषवत् पूर्ववत् सामान्यतो दृष्टं चेति ।
units.english: Inference is said to be of three kinds Pūrvavat a priori, Śeṣavat a posteriori and Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa commonly seen or analogous.

units.sanskrit: पूर्वमस्यास्तीति पूर्ववद् यथा मेघोन्नत्या वृष्टिं साधयति पूर्ववृष्टित्वात् ।
units.english: That which has got i.e., which is inferred from an antecedent i.e., cause is called Pūrvavat for example, one infers rain, seeing the rising cloud, as seen before.

units.sanskrit: शेषवद्यथा समुद्रादेकं जलपलं लवणमासाद्य शेषस्याप्यस्ति लवणभाव इति ।
units.english: Śeṣavat, for example, after finding a pala of water from the sea to be saltish, one infers that the rest of water is also saltish.

units.sanskrit: सामान्यतो दृष्टम् । देशान्तराद्देशान्तरं प्राप्तं दृष्टम् । गतिमच्चन्द्रतारकं चैत्रवत् ।
units.english: Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa, for example when the moon and the stars are observed to move from one place to another, one infers their locomotion, as in the case of Caitra.

units.sanskrit: यथा चैत्रनामानं देशान्तराद्देशान्तरं प्राप्तमवलोक्य गतिमानयामीति तद्वच्चन्द्रतारकमिति तथा पुष्पिताम्रदर्शनादन्यत्रपुष्पिताम्रा इति सामान्यतो दृष्टेन साधयति ।
units.english: Just as when one observes Caitra, leaving one place and reaching another, one infers that Caitra has locomotion, so have the moon and the stars locomotion. Similarly, observing a mango tree in blossom at a particular place, one infers that the mango trees are in blossom at other places also.

units.sanskrit: एतत्सामान्यदृष्टम् ।
units.english: This is Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa.

units.sanskrit: किञ्च तल्लिङ्गलिङ्गिपूर्वकमिति तदनुमानं लिङ्गपूर्वकं यत्र लिङ्गेन लिङ्गी अनुमीयते यथा दण्डेन यतिः ।
units.english: Moreover, it is preceded by the knowledge of linga the Middle term and the lingin the Major term. That inference is preceded by the knowledge of the Middle term, where a Major term is inferred by means of a Middle term e.g., by perceiving a staff, the possessor is inferred to be a mendicant.

units.sanskrit: लिङ्गिपूर्वकं च यत्र लिङ्गिना लिङ्गमनुमीयते यथा दृष्ट्वा यतिमस्येदं त्रिदण्डमिति ।
units.english: That preceded by a Major term iswhere a Middle term is inferred from the observation of a Major term e.g., seeing a mendicant, one infers that this triplestaff belongs to him.

units.sanskrit: आप्तश्रुतिराप्तवचनं च । आप्ता आचार्य्या ब्रह्मादयः ।
units.english: And Valid Testimony consists of the holy teachers and revelation Āpta, i.e., holy teachers, like Brahman and the rest.

units.sanskrit: श्रुतिर्वेदः ।
units.english: Śruti is the Veda.

units.sanskrit: आप्तश्च श्रुतिश्च आप्तश्रुती तदुक्तमाप्तवचनमिति ॥
units.english: The holy teachers and the Veda are called Āptaśruti. They are called Valid Testimony.

units.sanskrit: एवं त्रिविधं प्रमाणमुक्तं तत्र केन प्रमाणेन किं साध्यमुच्यते । सामान्यतस्तु दृष्टादतीन्द्रियाणां प्रसिद्धिरनुमानात् । तस्मादपि चासिद्धं परोक्षमाप्तागमात्सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: Thus three kinds of Means of Right Cognition have been defined. Now, it is explained what is to be proved by which Means of Right Cognition By means of Inference based on Analogy, the objects beyond senses are proved that which is not proved by this Inference and cannot be directly perceived, is proved, by Valid Testimony.

units.sanskrit: सामान्यतो दृष्टादनुमानादतीन्द्रियाणमिन्द्रियाण्यतीत्यवर्त्तमानानां सिद्धिः प्रधानपुरुषावतीन्द्रियौ सामान्यतो दृष्टेनानुमानेन साध्येते यस्मान्महदादिलिङ्गं त्रिगुणम् ।
units.english: By means of Inference based on Analogy, the objects beyond senses, i.e., the objects which cannot be directly perceived by the senses, are proved. Nature and the Spirit, which are beyond senseperception, are proved by inference based on analogy. For, the Middle term, Mahat and the rest, has three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: यस्येदं त्रिगुणं कार्यं तत्प्रधानमिति ।
units.english: Nature is that which has Mahat and the rest, possessing three Attributes, as its effect.

units.sanskrit: यतश्चातेनं चेतनमिवाभाति अतो ऽन्यो ऽधिष्ठाता पुरुष इति ।
units.english: Again, because, this Unconscious Nature appears to be conscious, therefore, it must have another, i.e., the conscious Spirit, to superintend it i.e., Nature.

units.sanskrit: व्यक्तं प्रत्यक्षसाध्यम् ।
units.english: Manifest is proved by Perception.

units.sanskrit: तस्मादपि चासिद्धं परोक्षमाप्तागमात् सिद्धं यथेन्द्रो देवराजः उत्तराः कुरवः स्वर्गे ऽप्सरस इति परोक्षमाप्तवचनात् सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: That which is not proved by this Inference and cannot be directly perceived, is proved by Valid Testimony. For exampleIndra, the king of gods the northern Kurus the nymphs in the Heaven all these imperceptibles are proved by Valid Testimony.

units.sanskrit: अत्र कश्चिदाह प्रधानः पुरुषो वा नोपलभ्यते यश्च नोपलभ्यते लोके तन्नास्ति तस्मात्तावपि न स्तः । यथा द्वितीयं शिरस्तृतीयो बाहुरिति ।
units.english: Here, somebody saysNature and the Spirit are not perceived that what is not perceived in this world, does not exist so Nature and the Spirit also do not exist for example, the second head or the third arm of a man do not exist.

units.sanskrit: तदुच्यते । अत्र सतामप्यर्थानामष्टधोपलब्धिर्न भवति तद्यथा ।
units.english: It is repliedIn this world, the nonperception of objects is caused by eight causes.

units.sanskrit: अतिदूरात्सामीप्यादिन्द्रियघातान्मनो ऽनवस्थानात् । सौक्ष्म्याद्व्यवधानादभिभवात्समानाभिहाराच्च ॥
units.english: They are On account of excessive distance, excessive proximity, injury to senses, inattention, minuteness, obstruction, suppression and mixture with what is similar, even the existent objects are not perceived.

units.sanskrit: इह सतामप्यर्थानामतिदूरादनुपलब्धिर्दृष्टा । यथा देशान्तरस्थानां चैत्रमैत्रविष्णुमित्राणाम् ।
units.english: Here, even existent objects are not perceived on account of excessive distance, for example, of Caitra, Maitra, and Viṣṇumitra living in another country.

units.sanskrit: सामीप्याद्यथा चक्षुषो ऽञ्जनानुपलब्धिः ।
units.english: On account of excessive proximity e.g., an eye cannot perceive collyrium in itself.

units.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाभिघाताद्यथा बधिरान्धयोः शब्दरूपानुपलब्धिः ।
units.english: On account of injury to senses e.g., deaf and blind men do not apprehend sound and colour.

units.sanskrit: सौक्ष्म्याद्यथा धूमोष्मजलनीहारपरमाणवो गगनगता नोपलभ्यन्ते ।
units.english: On account of minuteness e.g., the atoms of smoke, heat, water and frost are not visible in the sky.

units.sanskrit: व्यवधानाद्यथा कुड्येन पिहितं वस्तु नोपलभ्यते ।
units.english: On account of obstruction e.g., an object obstructed by a wall is invisible.

units.sanskrit: अभिभवाद्यथा सूर्यतेजसाभिभूता ग्रहनक्षत्रतारकादयो नोपलभ्यन्ते ।
units.english: On account of suppression e.g., the planets, asterisms, and stars are invisible on account of the suppression of their light by the sun.

units.sanskrit: समानाभिहाराद्यथा मुद्गराशौ मुद्गः क्षिप्तः कुवलयामलकमध्ये कुवलयामलके क्षिप्ते कपोतमध्ये कपोतो नोपलभ्यते सनानद्रव्यमध्याहृतत्वात् ।
units.english: On account of mixture with what is similar e.g., a grain of bean in a heap of beans, or a lotus and a myrabolan in a heap lotuses and myrabolans, and a pigeon in a flock of pigeons, are invisible, because, mixed with what is similar.

units.sanskrit: एवमष्टधानुपलब्धिः सतामर्थानामिह दृष्टा ॥
units.english: Thus, existent objects are not perceived in this world on account of these eight causes.

units.sanskrit: एवं चास्ति किमभ्युपगम्यते प्रधानपुरुषयोरप्येतयोर्वानुपलब्धिः केन हेतुना केन चोपलब्धिस्तदुच्यते । सौक्ष्म्यात्तदनुपलब्धिर्नाभावात्कार्यतस्तदुपलब्धिः ।
units.english: Thus, what is ascertained does exist. Now, it is explained why there is no apprehension of Nature and the Spirit, and how can they be apprehended The nonapprehension of Nature is due to its minuteness and not to nonexistence. It is ascertained from its effects.

units.sanskrit: महदादि तच्च कार्यं प्रकृतिविरूपं स्वरूपं च ॥
units.english: Those effects are Mahat and the rest, and they are similar and dissimilar to Nature.

units.sanskrit: सौक्ष्म्यात्तदनुपलब्धिः प्रधानस्येत्यर्थः ।
units.english: Its nonapprehension is due to minuteness. Nonapprehension of Nature.

units.sanskrit: प्रधानं सौक्ष्म्यान्नोपलभ्यते यथाकाशे धूमोष्मजलनीहारपरमाणवः सन्तो ऽपि नोपलभ्यन्ते ।
units.english: Nature is not apprehended on account of minuteness. As even the existent atoms of smoke, heat, water and frost are invisible in the sky.

units.sanskrit: कथं तर्हि तदुपलब्धिः । कार्यतस्तदुपलब्धिः ।
units.english: Then, how is it to be ascertained? It is to be ascertained from its effects.

units.sanskrit: कार्यण दृष्ट्वा कारणमनुमीयते ।
units.english: A cause is inferred from the observation of an effect.

units.sanskrit: अस्ति प्रधानं कारणं यस्येदं कार्यम् । बुद्धिरहंकारपञ्चतन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चमहाभूतानि एव तत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Nature, as the cause, does exist, whose effects are these intellect, ego, the five subtle elements, the eleven organs and the five gross elements they are the effects of that Nature.

units.sanskrit: तच्च कार्यं प्रकृतिविरूपम् । प्रकृतिः प्रधानं तस्य विरूपं प्रकृतेरसदृशं स्वरूपं च समानरूपं च तथा लोके ऽपि पितुस्तुल्य एव पुत्रो भवत्यतुल्यश्च ।
units.english: Those effects are dissimilar to Nature.Prakṛti is Nature dissimilar to it, i.e., dissimilar to Nature. And similarand similar in form. Even in this world, a son is similar as well as dissimilar to his father.

units.sanskrit: येन हेतुना तुल्यमतुल्यं तदुपरिष्टाद्वक्ष्यामः ॥
units.english: The causes of similarity and dissimilarity, we shall explain later on.

units.sanskrit: यदिदं महदादिकार्यं तत्किं प्रधाने सदुतादहोस्विदसदाचार्यविप्रतिपत्तेरयं संशयः । यतो ऽत्र सांख्यदर्शने सत्कार्यं बौद्धादीनामसत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Are all these effects, viz., Mahat and the rest, existent or nonexistent in their cause, i.e. Nature?For in this school of Sāmkya philosophy, the effect is existent with the Buddhists and the rest, it is nonexistent.

units.sanskrit: यदि सदसन्न भवत्यसत्सन्न भवतीति विप्रतिषेधस्तत्राह ।
units.english: If it is existent, it cannot be nonexistent if, however, it is nonexistent, then it cannot be existent. This is a contradiction.

units.sanskrit: असदकरणादुपादानग्रहणात्सर्वसम्भवाभावात् । शक्तस्य शक्यकरणात्कारणभावाच्च सत्कार्यम् ॥
units.english: Therefore, it is said The effect is existent in its cause, since, nonexistent cannot be produced, since the material cause is selected, since everything cannot be produced from anything, since a potent cause produces that of which it is capable and since effect is of the same nature as the cause.

units.sanskrit: असदकरणान्न सदसतो ऽकरणं तस्मात्सत्कार्यं इहलोके ऽसत्करणं नास्ति यथा सिकताभ्यस्तैलोत्पत्तिस्तस्मात्सतः करणादस्ति प्रागुत्पप्तेः ।
units.english: Since there can be no production of nonexistent thing, so an effect does exist in its cause. In this world we do not see the production of a nonexistent object, as oil cannot be produced from sand wherein oil is nonexistent.

units.sanskrit: प्रधाने व्यक्तमतः सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: So, since only an existent object can be produced, the Manifest does exist before its production in Nature.

units.sanskrit: किं चान्यदुपादानग्रहणादुपादानं कारणं तस्य ग्रहणादिहलोके यो येनार्थी स तदुपादानग्रहणं करोति दध्यर्थी क्षीरस्य न तु जलस्य तस्मात् सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Morever, since the material cause is selected Upādāna is the material cause on account of selecting it. In this world, a man selects the material cause of that thing which he wants. One who wants curds selects milk and not water.

units.sanskrit: इतश्च सर्वसम्भवाभावात् सर्वस्य सर्वत्रसम्भवो नास्ति यथा सुवर्णस्य रजतादौ तृणपांशुसिकतासु तस्मात् सर्वसम्भवाभावात् सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Therefore, the effect exists. Again, since everything cannot be produced. Everything cannot be produced from anywhere. For example, gold cannot be produced from silver, grass, dust and sand. So the effect is existent, because everything cannot be produced from anywhere.

units.sanskrit: इतशच शक्तस्य शक्यकरणात् ।
units.english: And again, since a potent thing can produce that of which it is capable.

units.sanskrit: इह कुलालः शक्तो मृद्दण्डचक्रचीवररज्जुनीरादिकरणोपकरणं वा शक्यमेव घटां मृत्पिण्डादुत्पादयति तस्मात् सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Here we see that only a potent thing, like the potter or the means like earth, wheel, a thread of rags, water etc., can produce, from the earth a pot, which is capable of being produced.

units.sanskrit: इतश्च कारणभावाच्च सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: Therefore, the effect is existent.

units.sanskrit: कारणं यल्लक्षणं तल्लक्षणमेव कार्यमेव यथा यवेभ्यो ऽपि यवाः व्रीहीभ्यो व्रीहयः यदासत्कार्यं स्यात्ततः कोद्रवेभ्यः शालयः स्युर्न च सन्तीति तस्मात् सत्कार्यम् ।
units.english: And also, since the effect is of the same nature as that cause. The effect is of the same nature of which the cause is e.g., barley is produced from barley and rice from rice. If the effect were not existent, then rice could be produced from kodravas and as it is not so, therefore, the effect is existent.

units.sanskrit: एवं पञ्चभिर्हेतुभिः प्रधाने महदादिलिङ्गमस्ति तस्मात्सत उत्पत्तिर्नासत इति ॥
units.english: Thus, there are five causes proving the existence of the mergent, viz., Mahat and the rest, in Nature.

units.sanskrit: प्रकृतिविरूपं सरूपं च यदुक्तं कथमित्युच्यते । हेतुमदनित्यमव्यापि सक्रियमनेकमाश्रितं लिङ्गम् ।
units.english: Now he explains the similarity and dissimilarity of Mahat and the rest with Nature The Manifest is caused, noneternal, nonpervading, active, manifold, dependent, mergent, conjunct and subordinate.

units.sanskrit: सावयवं परतन्त्रं व्यक्तं विपरीतमव्यक्तम् ॥
units.english: The Unmanifest is just the reverse.

units.sanskrit: व्यक्तं महदादिकार्य्यं हेतुमदिति हेतुरस्यास्ति हेतुमत् ।
units.english: The Manifest, viz., the effect like Mahat and the rest, is caused. Hetumat is that which has got a cause.

units.sanskrit: उपादानं हेतुः कारणं निमित्तमिति पर्यायाः ।
units.english: Upādāna, Heta, Kāraṇa and Nimitta are synonyms.

units.sanskrit: व्यक्तस्य प्रधानं हेतुरस्ति अतो हेतुमद्व्यक्तं भूतपर्य्यन्तं हेतुमद्बुद्धिमत्त्वं प्रधानेन हेतुमानहंकारो बुद्ध्या पञ्चतन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि हेतुमन्त्यहंकारेण । आकाशं शब्दतन्मात्रेण हेतुमत् । वायुः स्पर्शतन्मात्रेण हेतुमान् । तेजो रूपतन्मात्रेण हेतुमत् ।
units.english: The Manifest has Nature for its cause therefore, the entire Manifest up to the five gross elements, is caused. The principle of intellect is caused by Nature the principle of ego is caused by intellect the five subtle elements and the eleven organs are caused by the ego sky is caused by the subtle element of sound wind is caused by the subtle element of touch glow is caused by the subtle element of colour water is caused by the subtle element of taste earth is caused by the subtle element of smell.

units.sanskrit: एवं भूतपर्य्यन्तं व्यक्तं हेतुमत् ।
units.english: Thus, the entire Manifest up to the five gross elements is caused.

units.sanskrit: किं चान्यदनित्यं यस्मादन्यस्मादुत्पद्यते यथा मृत्पिण्डादुत्पद्यते घटः स चानित्यः ।
units.english: Again, it is noneternal because it is produced from another. For example, a jar is noneternal, because it is produced from a lump of clay.

units.sanskrit: किं चाव्याप्यसर्व्वगमित्यर्थः यथा प्रधानपुरुषौ सर्व्वगतौ नैव व्यक्तम् ।
units.english: Again, it is nonpervading that is, it is not allpervading. The Manifest is not allpervading as the Nature and the Spirit are.

units.sanskrit: किंचान्यत् सक्रियं संसारकाले संसरति त्रयोदशविधेन करणेन संयुक्तं सूक्ष्मं शरीरमाश्रित्य संसरति तस्मात् सक्रियम् ।
units.english: Again, it is active it migrates at the time of creation. Because, it migrates along with the subtle body endowed with thirteen instruments, it is active.

units.sanskrit: किंचान्यदनेकं बुद्धिरहंकारः पञ्चतन्मात्रान्येकादशेन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चमहाभूतानि पञ्चतन्मात्राश्रितानि ।
units.english: Again, it is manifold viz., intellect, ego, the five subtle elements, the eleven organs and the five gross elements. Again, it is dependent, i.e., dependent on its cause intellect depends upon Nature, ego depends upon intellect, the eleven organs and the five subtle elements depend upon ego and the five gross elements depend upon the five subtle elements.

units.sanskrit: किंच लिङ्गं लययुक्तं लयकाले पञ्चमहाभूतानि तन्मात्रेषु लीयन्ते तान्येकादशेन्द्रियैः सहाहंकारे स च बुद्धौ सा च प्रधाने लयं यातीति ।
units.english: It is endowed with the characteristic of merging. At the period of dissolution the five gross elements merge in five subtle elements the latter along with the eleven organs merge in ego ego merges in the intellect and the intellect merges in the Nature.

units.sanskrit: तथा सावयवं अवयवाः शब्दस्पर्शरसरूपगन्धाः तैः सह ।
units.english: Again, it is conjunct i.e. made up of parts sound, touch, taste, colour and smell are the parts endowed with them.

units.sanskrit: किंच परतन्त्रं नात्मनः प्रभवति यथा प्रधानतन्त्रा बुद्धिः बुद्धितन्त्रो ऽहंकारः अहंकारतन्त्राणि तन्मात्राणीन्द्रियाणि च तन्मात्रतन्त्राणि पञ्चमहाभूतानि च ।
units.english: Again, it is subordinate, i.e., it is not independent. As intellect is subordinate to Nature ego is subordinate to intellect the five subtle elements and the eleven organs are subordinate to ego and the five gross elements are subordinate to the five subtle elements.

units.sanskrit: एवं परतन्त्रं परायत्तं व्याख्यातं व्यक्तम् ।
units.english: Thus, the Manifest which is subordinate, dependent on another, is explained.

units.sanskrit: अथो ऽव्यक्तं व्याख्यामः ।
units.english: Now, we shall describe the Unmanifest.

units.sanskrit: विपरीतमव्यक्तम् । एतैरेव गुणैर्यथोक्तैर्विपरीतमव्यक्तं हेतुमद्व्यक्तमुक्तम् ।
units.english: The Unmanifest is the reverse, i.e., just the reverse of these characteristics belong to the Unmanifest. The Manifest has been described as caused.

units.sanskrit: नहि प्रधानात् परं किञ्चिदस्ति यतः प्रधानस्यानुत्पत्तिः तस्मादहेतुमदव्यक्तम् ।
units.english: There is nothing higher than Nature. And as the Nature is not produced, so the unmanifest is uncaused.

units.sanskrit: तथानित्यं च व्यक्तं नित्यमव्यक्तमनुत्पाद्यत्वात् नहि भूतानि कुतश्चिदुत्पद्यन्तेति प्रधानम् ।
units.english: Similarly, the Manifest is noneternal the Unmanifest is eternal, because not produced. It is not produced from anything like the gross elements. So, it is eternal.

units.sanskrit: किं चाव्यापि व्यक्तं व्यापि प्रधानं कार्य्यं स्यात् ।
units.english: There is nothing higher than the Nature of which the Nature could be an effect.

units.sanskrit: तथा व्यक्तं लिङ्गमलिङ्गमव्यक्तं नित्यत्वान्महदादि लिङ्गं प्रलयकाले परस्परं प्रलीयते नैवं प्रधानं तस्मादलिङ्गं प्रधानम् ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is mergent the Unmanifest is nonmergent, because it is eternal. The mergent, Mahat, etc., merge in one another at the time of dissolution. But the Nature is not such. Therefore, the Nature is nonmergent.

units.sanskrit: तथा सावयवं व्यक्तं निरवयवमव्यक्तं नहि शब्दस्पर्शरसरूपगन्धाः प्रधाने सन्ति ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is conjunct the Unmanifest is without parts. Sound, touch, taste, colour and smell do not exist in the Nature.

units.sanskrit: तथा परतन्त्रं व्यक्तं स्वतन्त्रमव्यक्तं प्रभवत्यात्मनः ॥
units.english: Again. the Manifest is subordinate the Unmanifest is independent, is its own master.

units.sanskrit: एवं व्यक्ताव्यक्तयोर्वैधर्म्म्यमुक्तं साधर्म्म्यमुच्यते यदुक्तं सरूपं च ।
units.english: Thus, the dissimilarity between the Manifest and the Unmanifest has been described now, the similarity between the two is explained, as it was said that it i.e. the product of the Nature is also similar to the Nature.

units.sanskrit: त्रिगुणमविवेकि विषयः सामान्यमचेतनं प्रसवधर्मि ।
units.english: The Manifest is composed of the three Attributes, nondiscriminated, objective, general, nonintelligent and productive.

units.sanskrit: व्यक्तं तथा प्रधानं तद्विपरीतस्तथा च पुमान् ॥
units.english: So also is the Nature. The Spirit is the reverse of that, as well as similar.

units.sanskrit: त्रिगुणं व्यक्तं सत्त्वरजस्तमांसि त्रयो गुणा यस्येति ।
units.english: The Manifest is composed of the three Attributes. It has the three Attributes, viz., Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

units.sanskrit: अविवेकि व्यक्तं न विवेको ऽस्यास्तीति ।
units.english: The Manifest is nondiscriminated that is, it is devoid of discrimination.

units.sanskrit: इदं व्यक्तमिमे गुणा इति न विवेककर्त्तुं याति अयं गौरयमश्व इति यथा ये गुणास्तद्व्यक्तं यद्व्यक्तं ते च गुणा इति ।
units.english: It is not possible to discriminate between the two that this is the Manifest and these are the Attributes, as we can do in the case of a bull and a horse that this is a bull and this is a horse.

units.sanskrit: तथा विषयो व्यक्तं भोज्यमित्यर्थः सर्वपुरुषाणां विषयभूतत्वात् ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is objective that is, it is an object of enjoyment because, it is an object of enjoyment for all the Spirits.

units.sanskrit: तथा सामान्यं व्यक्तं मूल्यदासीवत् सर्वसाधारणत्वात् ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is general because, it is common to all the Spirits like a harlot.

units.sanskrit: अचेतनं व्यक्तं सुखदुःखमोहान्न चेतयतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: The Manifest is nonintelligent that is, it is not conscious of pleasure, pain and delusion.

units.sanskrit: तथा प्रसवधर्मि व्यक्तं तद्यथा बुद्धेरहंकारः प्रसूयते तस्मात् पञ्चतन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि च प्रसूयन्ते तन्मात्रेभ्यः पञ्चमहाभूतानि ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is productive. For example, from intellect, ego is produced from ego, the five subtle elements and the eleven organs are produced from the five subtle elements, the five gross elements are produced.

units.sanskrit: एवमेते व्यक्तधर्माः प्रसवधर्मान्ता उक्ता एवमेभिरव्यक्तं सरूपं यथा व्यक्तं तथा प्रधानमिति ।
units.english: Thus, these characteristics of the Manifest ending with productiveness have been described. The Unmanifest is similar in these characteristics.As the manifest is, so also is the Nature.

units.sanskrit: तत्र त्रिगुणं व्यक्तमव्यक्तमपि त्रिगुणं यस्यैतन्महदादि कार्यं त्रिगुणम् ।
units.english: The Manifest is composed of the three Attributes the Unmanifest, whose products, viz., Mahat and the rest, are composed of the three Attributes, is also composed of the three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: इह यदात्मकं कारणं तदात्मकं कार्यमिति यथा कृष्णतन्तुकृतः कृष्ण एव पटो भवति ।
units.english: In this world, the effect has the same essence as the cause has e.g., a piece of cloth woven out of black yarn will be black.

units.sanskrit: तथाविवेकि व्यक्तं प्रधानमपि गुणैर्न भिद्यते अन्ये गुणा अन्यत् प्रधानमेव विवक्तुं न याति तदविवेकि प्रधानम् ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is nondiscriminated the Nature also cannot be discriminated from the three Attributes, It is not possible to discriminate that the Nature is other than the three Attributes so the Nature is nondiscriminated.

units.sanskrit: तथा विषयो व्यक्तं प्रधानमपि सर्वपुरुषविषयभूतत्वाद्विषय इति ।
units.english: Again the Manifest is objective the Nature also is objective, because it is an object of enjoyment for all the Spirits.

units.sanskrit: तथा सामान्यं व्यक्तं प्रधानमपि सर्वसाधारणत्वात् ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is general so also is the Nature, being common to all.

units.sanskrit: तथाचेतनं व्यक्तं प्रधानमपि सुखदुःखमोहान्न चेतयतीति कथमनुमीयत इह ह्यचेतनान्मृत्पिण्डादचेतनो घटा उत्पद्यते ।
units.english: Again, the Manifest is nonintelligent the Nature also is not conscious of pleasure, pain and delusion. How do you infer this?We see that from a nonintelligent lump of clay, a nonintelligent jar is produced.

units.sanskrit: एवं प्रधानमपि व्याख्यातम् ।
units.english: Thus the Nature also has been described.

units.sanskrit: इदानीं तद्विपरीतस्तथा पुमानित्येतद्व्याख्यायते । सद्विपरीतस्ताभ्यां व्यक्ताव्यक्ताभ्यां विपरीतः पुमान् ।
units.english: Now, we are going to explain“the Spirit is the reverse oof that as well as similar.” The reverse of that, i.e., the Spirit is the reverse o f the Manifest and the Unmanifest.

units.sanskrit: तद्यथा त्रिगुणं व्यक्तमव्यक्तं चागुणः पुरुषः ।
units.english: For example The Manifest and the Unmanifest are compose of the three Attributes the Spirit is Attributeless.

units.sanskrit: अविवेकि व्यक्तमव्यक्तं च विवेकी पुरुषः । तथा विषयो व्यक्तमव्यक्तं चाविषयः पुरुषः ।
units.english: The Manifest and the Unmanifest are nondiscriminated the Spirit is discriminating. The Manifest and the Unmanifest are objective the Spirit is nonobjective.

units.sanskrit: तथा सामान्यं व्यक्तमव्यक्तं चासामान्यः पुरुषः ।
units.english: The Manifest and the Unmanifest are general the Spirit is nongeneral i.e., individual.

units.sanskrit: अचेतनं व्यक्तमव्यक्तं च चेतनः पुरुषः सुखदुःखमोहांश्चेतयति संजानीते तस्माच्चेतनः पुरुष इति ।
units.english: The Manifest and the Unmanifest are nonintelligent, the Spirit is conscious of pleasure, pain and delusion it knows them therefore, it is intelligent.

units.sanskrit: प्रसवधर्मि व्यक्तं प्रधानं चाप्रसवधर्मी पुरुषो नहि किञ्चित् पुरुषात् प्रसूयते ।
units.english: The Manifest and the Nature are productive the Spirit is nonproductive. Nothing is produced from the Spirit.

units.sanskrit: तस्मादुक्तं तद्विपरीतः पुमानिति ।
units.english: Therefore, it is said that the Spirit is the reverse of that.

units.sanskrit: तदुक्तं तथा च पुमानिति । तत् पूर्वस्यामार्यायां प्रधानमहेतुमद्यथा व्याख्यातं तथा च पुमान् तद्यथा हेतुमदननित्यमित्यादि व्यक्तं तद्विपरीतमव्यक्तं तत्र हेतुमद्व्यक्तमहेतुमत् प्रधानं तथा च पुमानहेतुमाननुत्पाद्यत्वात् ।
units.english: As to the remark that the Spirit is similar to that, it has been explained in the previous verse, viz., as the Nature is uncaused, so is the Spirit. It was said there that the Manifest is caused, noneternal and so on, the Unmanifest is the reverse of that. Here, the Manifest is caused the Unmanifest is uncaused so is the Spirit uncaused, because it is not produced.

units.sanskrit: अनित्यं व्यक्तं नित्यं प्रधानं तथा च नित्यः पुमान् ।
units.english: The Manifest is noneternal the Unmanifest is eternal so also is the Spirit eternal.

units.sanskrit: अक्रियः सर्वगतत्वादेव ।
units.english: The Manifest is active the Unmanifest is inactive so also is the Spirit inactive, again because, it is omnipresent.

units.sanskrit: अनेकं व्यक्तमेकमव्यक्तं तथा पुमान्यप्येकः ।
units.english: The Manifest is manifold the Unmanifest is one so also is the Spirit one.

units.sanskrit: आश्रितं व्यक्तमनाश्रितमव्यक्तं तथा च पुमाननाश्रितः । लिङ्गं व्यक्तमलिङ्गं प्रधानं तथा च पुमानप्यलिङ्गः । न क्वचिल्लीयत इति ।
units.english: The Manifest is dependent the Unmanifest is independent so also is the Spirit independent. The Manifest is mergent the Unmanifest is nonmergent so also is the Spirit nonmergent, because it does not merge anywhere.

units.sanskrit: सावयवं व्यक्तं निरवयवमव्यक्तं तथा च पुमान् निरवयवः ।
units.english: The Manifest is conjunct the Unmanifest is nonconjunct so also is the Spirit nonconjunct.

units.sanskrit: नहि पुरुषे शब्दादयो ऽवयवाः सन्ति ।
units.english: There are no parts in the shape of sound and the rest in the Spirit.

units.sanskrit: किंच परतन्त्रं व्यक्तं स्वतन्त्रमव्यक्तं तथा च पुमानपि स्वतन्त्रः । आत्मनः प्रभवतीत्यर्थः ।
units.english: And again, the Manifest is subordinate the Unmanifest is nonSubordinate so also is the Spirit nonsubordinate, i.e., is its own master.

units.sanskrit: एवमेतदव्यक्तपुरुषयोः साधर्म्यं व्याख्यातं पूर्वस्यामार्यायाम् ।
units.english: Thus, the similarity of the Unmanifest with the Spirit was explained in the previous verse.

units.sanskrit: व्यक्तप्रधानयोः साधर्म्यं पुरुषस्य वैधर्म्यं च त्रिगुणमविवेकीत्यादि प्रकृत्यार्यायां व्याख्यातम् ॥ तत्र यदुक्तं त्रिगुणमिति व्यक्तमव्यक्तं च तत् के ते गुणा इति तत् स्वरूपप्रतिपादनायेदमाह ।
units.english: It has been said that the Manifest and the Unmanifest are composed of three Attributes. Now, what are those three Attributes?The following is stated to explain their nature Kārilā XII The Attributes are of the nature of pleasure, pain and delusion they are adapted to illuminate, to activate and to restrain.

units.sanskrit: प्रीत्यप्रीतिविषादात्मकाः प्रकाशप्रवृत्तिनियमार्थाः । अन्यो ऽन्याभिभवाश्रयजननमिथुनवृत्तयश्च गुणाः ॥
units.english: They mutually suppress, support, produce, consort and exist. The Attributes, viz., Sattva, Rajas and Tamas are of the nature of pleasure, pain and delusion.

units.sanskrit: तत्र प्रीत्यात्मकं सत्त्वं प्रीतिः सुखं तदात्मकमिति ।
units.english: The Sattva is of the nature of prīti prīti is p]easure it is of this nature.

units.sanskrit: अप्रीत्यात्मकं रजः ।
units.english: The Rajas is of the nature of aprīti aprīti is pain.

units.sanskrit: विषादात्मकं तमः । विषादो मोहः ।
units.english: The Tamas is of the nature of viṣāda viṣāda is delusion.

units.sanskrit: तथा प्रकाशप्रवृत्ति नियमार्थाः ।
units.english: Again, they are adapted to illuminate, to activate and to restrain.

units.sanskrit: अर्थः शब्दः सामर्थ्यवाची प्रकाशार्थं सत्त्वं प्रकाशसमर्थमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: The word artha stands for ‘competency’. Ptakāśārtham Sattvam means ‘competent to illuminate’.

units.sanskrit: प्रवृत्त्यर्थं रजो नियमार्थं तमः स्थितौ समर्थमित्यर्थः प्रकाशक्रियास्थितिशीला गुणा इति ।
units.english: Rajas is adapted to activate. Tamas is adapted to restrain, i.e., is competent to fix a thing. That is, the Attributes are of the nature of illumination, activity and fixture.

units.sanskrit: तथान्योन्याभिभवाश्रयजननमिथुनवृत्तयश्च ।
units.english: Again,and they mutually suppress, support, produce, consort and exist.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्याभिभवाः अन्योन्याश्रयाः अन्योन्यजननाः अन्योन्यमिथुनाः अन्योन्यवृत्तयश्च ते तथोक्ताः ।
units.english: That is, they are mutually suppressive, mutually supporting, mutually productive, mutually consorting and mutually existing.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्याभिभवा इति अन्योन्यं परस्परमभिभवन्तीति प्रीत्यप्रीत्यादिभिर्धर्म्मैराविर्भवन्ति यथा यदा सत्त्वमुत्कटं भवति तदा रजस्तमसी अप्रीतिप्रवृत्तिधर्म्मेण यदा तमस्तदा सत्त्वरजसी विषादस्थित्यात्मकेन इति ।
units.english: Mutually suppressive they mutually, i.e., one another, suppress, i.e., manifest themselves with the characteristics of pleasure, pain, etc. That means,when Sattva is predominant, then it is so by suppressing the Rajas and Tamas with its characteristics and it exhibits itself as pleasure and illumination.

units.sanskrit: तथान्योन्याश्रयाश्च द्व्यणुकवद्गुणाः ।
units.english: And the Attributes are mutually supporting like a binary.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्यजननाः यथा मृत्पिण्डो घटं जनयति ।
units.english: They are mutually productive, as a lump of clay produces jar.

units.sanskrit: तथान्योन्यमिथुनाश्च यथा स्त्रीपुंसौ अन्योन्यमिथुनौ तथा गुणाः ।
units.english: And they are mutually consorting as husband and wife are mutually consorting, so are the Attributes.

units.sanskrit: उक्तं च । रजसो मिथुनं सत्त्वं सत्त्वस्य मिथुनं रजः । उभयोः सत्त्वरजरोर्मिथुनं तम उच्यते ॥
units.english: And it is said “The consort of Rajas is Sattva, the consort of Sattva is Rajas the consort of Sattva and Rajas, is said to be Tamas.” Devībhāgavata, III, .

units.sanskrit: परस्परसहाया इत्यर्थः ।
units.english: That is, they are the helpmates of one another.

units.sanskrit: अन्योन्यवृत्तयश्च परस्परं वर्त्तन्ते गुणाः गुणेषु वर्त्तन्त इति वचनात् ।
units.english: And, they mutually exist, i.e., they coexist, according to the text, “The Attributes exist in the Attributes,” Bhagavadgītā, III, .

units.sanskrit: यथा सुरूपा सुशीला स्त्री सर्व्वसुखहेतुः सपत्नीनां सैव दुःखहेतुः सैव रागिणां मोहं जनयति एव सत्वं रजस्तमसोर्वृत्तिहेतुर्यथा राजा सदोद्युक्तः प्रजापालने दुष्टनिग्रहे शिष्टानां सुखमुत्पादयति दुष्टानां दुःखं मोहं च एवं रजस्सत्त्वतमसोर्वृत्तिं जनयति ।
units.english: Just as a beautiful and virtuous woman is a source of pleasure to all but the same woman is a source of pain to her cowives and the same woman produces delusion in the passionate people similarly, Sattva is the source of the existence of Rajas and Tamas. Just as a king ever assiduous in protecting his subjects and punishing the wicked, produces pleasure in the good people and pain and delusion in the wicked, similarly, Rajas brings about the existence of Sattva and Tamas.

units.sanskrit: तथा तमः स्वरूपेणावरणात्मकेन सत्त्वरजसोर्वृत्तिं जनयति यथा मेघाः खमावृत्य जगतः सुखमुत्पादयन्ति ते वृष्ट्या कर्षुकाणां कर्षणोद्योगं जनयन्ति विरहिणां मोहमेवमन्योन्यवृत्तयो गुणाः ॥
units.english: In the same way, Tamas brings about the existence of Sattva and Rajas by its own nature of covering things. For example, the clouds, covering the sky, produce pleasure in the world they urge the farmer to activity by their rain, and produce delusion in the separated lovers.

units.sanskrit: किंचान्यत् ।
units.english: Thus, the Attributes are mutually existent.

units.sanskrit: सत्त्वं लघु प्रकाशकमिष्टमुपष्टम्भकं चलं च रजः ।
units.english: Moreover Sattva is considered to be light and bright, Rajas exciting and mobile, and Tamas is only heavy and enveloping.

units.sanskrit: गुरु वरणकमेव तमः प्रदीपवच्चार्थतो वृत्तिः ॥
units.english: Like a lamp, their function is to gain an end.

units.sanskrit: सत्त्वं लघु प्रकाशकं च यदा सत्त्वमुत्कटं भवति तदा लघून्यङ्गानि बुद्धिप्रकाशश्च प्रसन्नतेन्द्रियाणां भवति ।
units.english: Sattva is light and bright. When Sattva predominates then the limbs become light, the intellect becomes bright and the organs become clear i.e. acute.

units.sanskrit: उपष्टम्भकं चलं च रजः उपष्टम्भातीत्युपष्टम्भकमुद्योतकं यथा वृषो वृषदर्शने उत्कटमुपष्टम्भं करोति एव रजोवृत्तिः ।
units.english: Rajas is exciting and mobile. Upaṣṭambhaka is that which excites or stimulates. Just as a bull is very much excited at the sight of another bull, so is the nature of Rajas. And Rajas is observed to be mobile.

units.sanskrit: तथा रजश्च चलं दृष्टं रजोवृत्तिश्चलचित्तो भवति ।
units.english: A man of the nature of Rajas is fickleminded.

units.sanskrit: गुरु वरणमेकमेव तमः यदा तम उत्कटं भवति तदा गुरूण्यङ्गान्यावृतानीन्द्रियाणि भवन्ति स्वार्थासमर्थानि ।
units.english: Tamas is only heavy and enveloping. When Tamas predominates, then the limbs become heavy and the organs become enveloped i.e., dullincapable of apprehending their objects.

units.sanskrit: अत्राह यदि गुणाः परस्परं विरुद्धाः स्वमतेनैव कमर्थं निष्पादयन्ति तर्हि कथं प्रदीपवच्चार्थतो वृत्तिः प्रदीपेन तुल्यं प्रदीपवदर्थतः साधना वृत्तिरिष्टा यथा प्रदीपः परस्परविरुद्धतैलाग्निवर्त्तिसंयोगादर्थप्रकाशान् जनयति एवं सत्त्वरजस्तमांसि परस्परं विरुद्धान्यर्थं निष्पादयन्ति ॥
units.english: Here, one may askHow do the mutually opposed Attributes produce one common effect, although acting according to their own individual intentions?Reply, like a Lamp, their function is to gain an end. Pradīpavat means like a Lamp. Their function is considered to be aiming to achieve a common end. Just as a lamp composed of oil, fire and the wick, which are opposed to one another, illuminates objects, so Sattva, Rajas and Tamas, although opposed to one another, produce an effect.

units.sanskrit: अन्तरप्रश्नो भवति त्रिगुणमविवेकि विषय इत्यादि प्रधानं व्यक्तं च व्याख्यातं तत्र प्रधानमुपलभ्यमानं महदादि च त्रिगुणमविवेक्यादीति च कथमवगम्यते तत्राह ।
units.english: Another question arises here,you have explained that the Nature and the Manifest are “composed of the three Attributes, nondiscriminated and objective.” How do you know that the Nature, and the manifested Mahat, etc., are composed of the three Attributes, etc.?

units.sanskrit: अविवेक्यादिः सिद्धस्त्रैगुण्यात्तद्विपर्ययाभावात् ।
units.english: This is answered The qualities of nondiscriminatedness and the rest of the characteristics of the Manifest are proved to exist in the Manifest by the possession of the three Attributes and by the absence of its i.e. of the Manifest reverse.

units.sanskrit: कारणगुणात्मकत्वात्कार्यस्याव्यक्तमपि सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: The Unmanifest is also proved by the effect being of the same nature as its cause.

units.sanskrit: यो ऽयमविवेक्यादिर्गुणः स त्रैगुण्यान्महदादौ ऽव्यक्तेनायं सिद्ध्यति । अत्रोच्यते तद्विपर्ययाभावात्तस्य विपर्ययस्तद्विपर्ययस्तस्याभावस्तद्विपर्ययाभावस्तस्मात् सिद्धमव्यक्तम् ।
units.english: The characteristics of nondiscriminatedness and the rest exist in Mahat and the rest, because they are of the nature of the three Attributes but they i.e., the characteristics are not proved to exist in the Unmanifest.Therefore, it is saidBy the absence of its reverse the reverse of it, the absence thereof, i.e., the absence of the reverse thus the Unmanifest is proved.

units.sanskrit: यथा यत्रैव तन्तवस्तत्रैव पटः । अन्ये तन्तवो ऽन्यः पटो न कुतस्तद्विपर्ययाभावात् ।
units.english: For example, wherever there is yarn, there is cloth the yarn and the cloth are not different things Why? Because, there is absence of the reverse.

units.sanskrit: एवं व्यक्ताव्यक्तसम्पन्नो भवति दूरं प्रधानमासन्नं व्यक्तं यो व्यक्तं पश्यति स प्रधानमपि पश्यति तद्विपर्ययाभावात् ।
units.english: Thus, there is a relationship sambandha established between the Manifest and the Unmanifest. Far away is the Unmanifest, but the Manifest is at hand. So, one who sees the Manifest, sees also the Unmanifest because, there is the absence of its, reverse.

units.sanskrit: इतश्चाव्यक्तं सिद्धं कारणगुणात्मकत्वात् कार्यस्य ।
units.english: Hence also the Unmanifest is provedBecause of an effect being of the same nature as its cause.

units.sanskrit: लोके यदात्मकं कारणं तदात्मकं कार्यमपि तथा कृष्णेभ्यस्तन्तुभ्यः कृष्ण एव पटो भवति ।
units.english: We see in this world that whatever the essence of a cause, the same is that of the effect. Asfrom black yarn, only black cloth is produced.

units.sanskrit: एवं महदादिलिङ्गमविवेकिविषयः सामान्यचेतनं प्रसवधर्मि यदात्मकं लिङ्गं तदात्मकमव्यक्तमपि सिद्धम् ॥
units.english: Thus, the mergent Mahat and the rest are nondiscriminated, objective, general, nonintelligent and productive. So, whatever the essence of the mergent, the Unmanifest is also proved to possess the same essence.

units.sanskrit: त्रैगुण्यादविवेक्यादिर्व्यक्ते सिद्धस्तद्विपर्ययाभावात् । एवं कारणगुणात्मकत्वात् कार्यस्याव्यक्तमपि सिद्धमित्येतन्मिथ्या लोके यन्नोपलभ्यते तन्नास्ति एवं प्रधानमप्यस्ति किं तु नोपलभ्यते ।
units.english: “On account of the possession of the three Attributes, nondiscriminatedness and the rest are proved to exist in the Manifest By the absence of the reverse and by the effect being of the same nature as its cause, the Unmanifest is also proved”, this is false. Because, all what we do not apprehend in this world, does not exist.

units.sanskrit: भेदानां परिमाणात्समन्वयाच्छक्तितः प्रवृत्तेश्च । कारणकार्यविभागादविभागाद्वैश्वरूप्यस्य ॥ कारणमस्त्यव्यक्तमिति क्रियाकारकसम्बन्धः ।
units.english: The Unmanifest cause does exist, because of the finiteness of the specific objects, because of natural sequence, because of activity depending upon efficiency, because of distinction between cause and effect and because of the merging of this diverse evolved.

units.sanskrit: भेदानां परिमाणालोके यत्र कर्त्तास्ति तस्य परिमाणं दृष्टं यथा कुलालः परिमितैर्मृत्पिण्डैः परिमितानेव घटान् करोति एवं महदपि महदादिलिङ्गं परिमितं भेदतः प्रधानकार्यमेका बुद्धिरेको ऽहंकारः पञ्च तन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चतन्मात्राणि एकादशेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चमहाभूतानीत्येवं भेदानां परिमाणादस्ति प्रधानं कारणं यद्व्यक्तं परिमितमुत्पादयति ।यदि प्रधानं न स्यात्तदा निःपरिमाणमिदं व्यक्तमपि न स्यात् परिमाणाच्च भेदानामस्ति प्रधानं यस्माद्व्यक्तमुत्पन्नम् ।
units.english: Because of the finiteness of the specific objects. In this world, wherever, we find an agent, we see a finiteness of his. For example, a potter makes only finite jars from finite lumps of clay so does Mahat also. The mergent Mahat and the rest are finite and are the specific effects of the Nature. Intellect is one, ego is one, the subtle elements are five, the organs are eleven and the gross elements are five.Thus, on account of the finiteness of the specific objects, there is Nature as the cause which produces the finite Manifest.

units.sanskrit: तथा समन्वयादिह लोके प्रसिद्धिर्दृष्टा यथा व्रतधारिणं बटुं दृष्ट्वा समन्वयति नूनमस्य पितरौ ब्राह्मणाविति एवमिदं त्रिगुणं महदादिलिङ्गं दृष्ट्वा साधयामो ऽस्य यत् कारणं भविष्यतीति अतः समन्वयादस्ति प्रधानम् ।
units.english: And so, on account of the finiteness of the specific objects, there is Nature, wherefrom this Manifest has sprung up. Again, because of natural sequence. This is quite well known in this world that when one sees a boy engaged in performing sacred rites, one infers that his parents are naturally brahmins. Similarly, seeing this mergent i.e. the evolved, we arrive at a thing which must be its cause.

units.sanskrit: तथा शक्तितः प्रवृत्तेश्च इह यो यस्मिन् शक्तः स तस्मिन्नेवार्थे प्रवर्त्तते यथा कुलालो घटास्य करणे समर्थो घटमेव करोति न पटं रथं वा ।
units.english: Again, because of activity depending upon efficiency. Here a man does that for which he is efficient. For example, a potter who is efficient to produce a jar, produces only a jar and not cloth or chariot. Again.

units.sanskrit: तथास्ति प्रधानं कारणं कुतः कारणकार्यविभागात् ।
units.english: there is Nature as the cause. How?Because of distinction between cause and effect.

units.sanskrit: करोतीति कारणम् । क्रियत इति कार्यम् ।
units.english: Kāraṇa is that which produces kārya is that which is produced.

units.sanskrit: कारणस्य कार्यस्य च विभागो यथा घटो दधिमधूदकपयसां धारणे समर्थो न तथा तक्तारणं मृत्पिण्डः ।
units.english: There is a distinction of functions of cause and effect. For example, as a jar is competent to hold curds, honey, water and milk, so is not a lump of clay competent.

units.sanskrit: मृत्पिण्डो वा घटं निष्पादयति न चैवं घटो मृत्पिण्डम् ।
units.english: Or, a lump of clay produces a jar, but a jar does not produce lump of clay.

units.sanskrit: एवं महदादिलिङ्गं दृष्ट्वानुमीयते । अस्ति विभक्तं तत् कारणं यस्य विभाग इदं व्यक्तमिति ।
units.english: Thus, seeing the mergent Mahat and the rest, it is inferred that there is a separate cause from which this Manifest has separated i.e., evolved itself.

units.sanskrit: इतश्च अविभागाद्वैश्वरूपस्य विश्वं जगत् तस्य रूपं व्यक्तिः ।
units.english: And again, because of the merging of the diverse evoloved. Viśva means universe its rūpa is manifestation.

units.sanskrit: विश्वरूपस्य भावो वैश्वरूपं तस्याविभागादस्ति प्रधानं यस्मात्रैलोक्यस्य पञ्चानां पृथिव्यादीनां महाभूतानां परस्परं विभागो नास्ति महाभूतेष्वन्तर्भूतास्त्रयो लोका इति पृथिव्यापस्तेजोवायुराकाशमिति एतानि पञ्चमहाभूतानि प्रलयकाले सृष्टिक्रमेणैवाविभागं यान्ति तन्मात्रेषु परिणामिषु तन्मात्राण्येकादशेन्द्रियाणि चाहंकारे अहंकारो बुद्धौ बुद्धिः प्रधाने एवं त्रयो लोकाः प्रलयकाले प्रकृतावविभागं गच्छन्ति तस्मादविभागात् क्षीरदधिवद्व्यक्ताव्यक्तयोरव्यक्तं कारणम् ॥
units.english: The abstraction of viśvarūpa is vaiśvarūpya i.e., manifested or evolved on account of its merging there is Nature because there is no mutual distinction between the three worlds and the five gross elements,i.e. the three worlds are included in the five gross elements. At the time of dissolution, the five gross elements, viz., earth, water, fire, air and ether, merge into the modified five subtle elements in the order of creation the five subtle elements and the eleven organs merge into ego ego merges into intellect intellect merges into Nature. Thus, the three worlds merge into Nature at the time of dissolution. From such merging of the Manifest and the Unmanifest, like that of milk and curds, there does exist the Unmanifest as the cause.

units.sanskrit: अतश्च ।
units.english: And for this reason The Unmanifest as the cause does exist.

units.sanskrit: कारणमस्त्यव्यक्तं प्रवर्तते त्रिगुणतः समुदयाच्च । परिणामतः सलिलवत्प्रतिप्रतिगुणाश्रयविशेषात् ॥
units.english: It functions through the three Attributes by combining and by modification, like water, due to the particular characteristics of the abode of each of the Attributes.

units.sanskrit: अव्यक्तं प्रख्यातं कारणमस्ति यस्मान्महदादिलिङ्गं प्रवर्त्तते ।
units.english: The wellknown Unmanifest as the cause does exist from which proceed the mergent Mahat and the rest.

units.sanskrit: त्रिगुणतः त्रिगुणात् सत्त्वरजस्तमोगुणा यस्मिंस्तत्त्रिगुणं तत्किमुक्तं भवति सत्त्वरजस्तमसां साम्यावस्था प्रधानम् ।
units.english: Triguṇataḥ.i.e., from the Nature possessed of the three Attributes. Triguṇa is that which has the three Attributes, viz., Sattva, Rajas and Tamas. Then, what is the sense?It isthat the Nature is the equilibrium of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

units.sanskrit: तथा समुदयात् यथा गंगाश्रोतांसि त्रिणी रुद्रमूर्द्धनि पतितानि एकं स्रोतो जनयति एवं त्रिगुणमव्यक्तमेकं व्यक्तं जनयति तथा वा तन्तवः समुदिताः पटं जनयन्ति एवमव्यक्तं गुनसमुदयान्महदादि जनयतीति त्रिगुणतः समुदयाच्च व्यक्तं जगत् प्रवर्त्तते ।
units.english: Again, by combining. As the three streams of the Ganges falling on the head of Rudra, combine to produce one stream, so the Unmanifest endowed with the three Attributes produces one Manifest. Or, as the combined threads produce cloth, so the Unmanifest creates Mahat and the rest, on account of the combination of the three Attributes. So, the manifested universe proceeds from the three Attributes and their combination.

units.sanskrit: यस्मादेकस्मात् प्रधानाद्व्यक्तं तस्मादेकरूपेण भवितव्यम् ।
units.english: Well, as the entire Manifest proceeds from one Nature, so the former must be uniform.This objection does not arise.

units.sanskrit: नैष दोषः परिणामतः सलिलवत् प्रतिप्रतिगुणाश्रयविशेषादेकस्मात् प्रधानात् त्रयो लोकाः समुत्पन्नास्तुल्यभावा न भवन्ति देवाः सुखेन युक्ता मनुष्या दुःखेन तिर्यञ्चो मोहेन एकस्मात् प्रधानात् प्रवृत्तं व्यक्तं प्रतिप्रतिगुणाश्रयविशेषात् परिणमातः सलिलवद्भवति ।
units.english: Because by modification, like water, due to the particular characteristics of abode of each of the Attributes. The three worlds born of one Nature are not of uniform nature. Gods are happy, men are unhappy and the animals are deluded. The Manifest, proceeding from one Unmanifest, becomes like water on account of modification based on the particular characteristics abiding in each of the three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: गुणानामाश्रयो गुणाश्रयस्तद्विशेषस्तं गुणाश्रयविशेषं प्रतिनिधाय प्रतिप्रतिगुणाश्रयविशेषं परिणामात् प्रवर्त्तते व्यक्तं यथा आकाशादेकरसं सलिलं पतितं नानारूपात्संश्लेषाद्भिद्यते तद्रसान्तरैरेवमेकस्मात् प्रधानात् प्रवृत्तास्त्रयो लोका नैकस्वभावा भवन्ति देवेषु सत्त्वमुत्कटं रजस्तमसी उदासीने तेन ते ऽत्यन्तसुखिनो मनुष्येषु रज उत्कटं भवति सत्त्वतमसी उदासीने तेन ते ऽत्यन्तदुःखिनो तिर्यक्षु तम उत्कटं भवति सत्त्वजसी उदासीने तेन ते ऽत्यन्तमूढाः ॥
units.english: The repetition of prati denotes “succession.” Guṇāśraya means the abode of the Attributes its particular characteristic.Taking into consideration the particular characteristics of the abode of the three Attributes, the Manifest is created from the modification based upon the particular characteristics of the abode of the three Attributes. For example, water falling from the sky is of uniform nature but coming into contact with different forms, that water becomes of different forms, due to different tastes. Similarly, the three worlds proceeding from one Nature, are not of uniform nature. Among the gods, the Sattva is predominant, and Rajas and Tamas are indifferent so they are very happy. Among men, the Rajas is predominant, and Sattva and Tamas are indifferent therefore, they are very unhappy, Among animals the Tamas is predominant, and Sattva and Rajas are indifferent so they are very insensible.

units.sanskrit: एवमार्याद्वयेन प्रधानस्यास्तित्वमभ्युपगम्यते ।
units.english: Thus, by these two verses, the existence of the Nature is known.

units.sanskrit: इतश्चोत्तरं पुरुषास्तित्वप्रतिपादनार्थमाह । सङ्घातपरार्थत्वात्त्रिगुणादिविपर्ययादधिष्ठानात् । पुरुषो ऽस्ति भोक्तृभावात्कैवल्यार्थप्रवृत्तेश्च ॥
units.english: Now, after this, the author proceeds to prove the existence of the Spirit The Spirit exists, since composite objects are meant for another since it is the reverse of that which has the three Attributes and the rest since there must be control since there must he someone who enjoys and since there is activity for release.

units.sanskrit: यदुक्तं व्यक्ताव्यक्तविज्ञानान्मोक्षः प्राप्यत इति तत्र व्यक्तादनन्तरमव्यक्तं पञ्चभिः कारणैरधिगतमव्यक्तवत् पुरुषो ऽपि सूक्ष्मस्तस्याधुनानुमितास्तित्वं प्रतिक्रियते ।
units.english: It had been pointed out that the release is obtained by the discriminative knowledge of the Manifest, the Unmanifest and the Knower. So, after the knowledge of the Manifest, the Unmanifest has been known to exist by five reasons verse . Like the Unmanifest the Spirit also is subtle.

units.sanskrit: अस्ति पुरुषः कस्मात् संघातपरार्थत्वात् ।
units.english: The Spirit exists. How?Since composite objects are meant for another.

units.sanskrit: यो ऽयं महदादि संघातः स पुरुषार्थ इत्यनुमीयते अचेतनत्वात् पर्यङ्गवत् ।
units.english: It is inferred that the composition of Mahat and the rest is meant for the Spirit, because, it i.e., composition is unconscious like a bed.

units.sanskrit: यथा पर्यङ्क प्रत्येकं गात्रोत्पलकपादवटतूलीप्रछादनपटोपधानसंघतः परार्थो नहि स्वार्थः पर्यङ्कस्य नहि किञ्चिदपि गात्रोत्पलाद्यवयवानां परस्परं कृत्यमस्ति ।
units.english: For example. a bedis composed of gātrotpalaka?, a footstool, a covering cloth of cotton and a pillow it serves another person’s purpose and not its own. The different parts, viz., gātrotpalaka, etc., of the bed cannot serve any mutual purpose.

units.sanskrit: अतो ऽवगम्यते ऽस्ति पुरुषो यः पर्यङ्के शेते यस्यार्थं पर्यङ्कस्तत्परार्थमिदं शरीरं पञ्चानां महाभूतानां संघातो वर्त्तते ऽस्ति पुरुषो यस्येदं भोग्यशरीरं भोग्यं महदादिसंघातरूपं समुत्पन्नमिति ।
units.english: So, it is inferred that there is a man who sleeps on the bed,for whom this bed is meant. So, this body, a composite of five gross elements, is meant for another. There exists the Spirit for whom this enjoyable body is born the body which is a composite of Mahat and the rest.

units.sanskrit: इतश्चात्मास्ति त्रिगुणादिविपर्ययात् यदुक्तं पूर्वस्यामार्यायां त्रिगुनमविवेकिविषय इत्यादि । तस्माद्विपर्ययाद्येनोक्तं तद्विपरीतस्तथा पुमान् ।
units.english: Hence also, the Spirit existssince it is the rerverse of that which has the three Attributes, viz., “possessed of the three Attributes, nondiscriminated, objective, etc.,” mentioned in the previous verse,the reverse of this.

units.sanskrit: अधिष्ठानाद्यथेह लंघनल्पवनधावनसमर्थैरश्वैर्युक्तो रथः सारथिनाधिष्ठितः प्रवर्त्तते तथात्माधिष्ठानाच्छरीरमिति ।
units.english: As here, a chariot, united to horses capable of leaping, galloping and running, functions only when controlled by a charioteer, so does the body function on account of the control of the Spirit.

units.sanskrit: तथा चोक्तं षष्ठितन्त्रे पुरुषाधिष्ठितं प्रधानं प्रवर्त्तते । अतो ऽस्त्यात्माभोक्तृत्वात् ।
units.english: As it is said in the Ṣaṣṭitantra“The Nature functions when controlled by the Spirit.” Hence, the Spirit exists.Since there must be someone who enjoys.

units.sanskrit: यथा मधुराम्ललवणकटुतिक्तकषायषड्रसोपबृंहित्स्य संय्क्तस्यान्नस्य साध्यते एवं महदादिलिङ्गस्य भोक्तृत्वाभावादस्ति स आत्मा यस्येदं भोग्यं शरीरम्ति ।
units.english: For example, we infer that there must be an enjoyer of mixed food flavoured with the six flavours, viz., sweet, sour, salt, pungent, bitter and astringent similarly, because the mergent Mahat and the rest are not enjoyers, we infer that the Spirit exists,for whose enjoyment this body is.

units.sanskrit: इतश्च कैवल्यार्थम प्रवृत्तेश्च केवलस्य भावः कैवल्यं तन्निमितं या च प्रवृत्तिस्तस्याः स्वकैवल्यार्थं प्रवृत्तेः सकाशादनुमीयते अस्त्यात्मेति यतो सर्वो विद्वानविद्वांश्च संसारसन्तानक्षयमिच्छति ।
units.english: Hence, also the Spirit exists , since there is activity for release. Kaivalya is the abstraction of kevala alone the activity for this purpose from this activity for its own release, it is inferred that the Spirit exists. For, everybody, learned or otherwise, desires for the cessation of the cycle of his births and deaths.

units.sanskrit: एवमेभिर्हेतुभिरस्त्यात्मा शरीराद्व्यतिरिक्तः ॥
units.english: For these reasons there exists the Spirit apart from the body.

units.sanskrit: अथ स किमेकह सर्वशरीरे ऽधिष्ठाता मणिरसनात्मकसूत्रवत् आहोस्विद्बहव आत्मानः प्रतिशरीरमधिष्ठातार इत्यत्रोच्यते । जन्ममरणकरणानां प्रतिनियमादयुगपत्प्रवृत्तेश्च । पुरुषबहुत्वं सिद्धं त्रैगुण्यविपर्ययाच्चैव ॥
units.english: “Is that Spirit one, controlling all the bodies like a string passing through a chain of jewels, or are there many Spirits controlling each body?”To this is replied The plurality of the Spirits is established, because birth, death and organs are allotted separately because there is no activity at one time, and because there are different modifications of the three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: जन्म च मरणं च करणानि च जन्ममरणकरणानि तेषां प्रतिनियमात् प्रत्येकनियमादित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Janmamaraṇakaraṇāni, means birth, death and the organs because of their pratiniyama, i.e., separate allotment of each.

units.sanskrit: यद्येक एव आत्मा स्यात्तत एकस्य जन्मनि सर्व एव जायेरन् एकस्य मरणे सर्वे ऽपि म्रियेरन् एकस्य करणवैकल्ये बाधिर्यान्धमूकत्वकुणत्वखंजत्वलक्षणे सर्वे ऽपि बधिरान्धकुणिखंजाः स्युर्न चैवं भवति तस्माज्जन्ममरणकरणानां प्रतिनियमात् पुरुषबहुत्वं सिद्धम् ।
units.english: If there were one Spirit, then when one Spirit were to be born, all would be born or when one were to die all would die or when one were to have any organic defect in the shape of deafness, blindness, dumbness, mutilation or lameness, then all would be deaf, blind, mutilated or lame. But it does not happen so. Therefore, because birth, death and the organs are allotted separately, the plurality of the Spirits is established. Again, because there is no activity at one time.

units.sanskrit: इतश्चायुगपत् प्रवृत्तेश्च युगपदेककालं न युगपदयुगपत् प्रवर्त्तनं यस्मादयुगपद्धर्मादिषु प्रवृत्तिर्दृश्यते एके धर्मे प्रवृत्ता अन्ये ऽधर्मे वैराग्ये ऽन्ये ज्ञाने ऽन्ये प्रवृत्ताः तस्मादयुगपत् प्रवृत्तेश्च बहव इति सिद्धम् ।
units.english: Yugapat means at one time ayugapat, i.e., not at one time, pravartanam. i.e. activity. Because we see that all people are not engaged in virtue and the rest at one and the same time. Some are engaged in virtue, others in vice, some in renunciation and some in knowledge. Therefore, by there being no activity at one time, ‘there are many Spirits’ is proved.

units.sanskrit: किञ्चान्यत्त्रैगुण्याविपर्ययाच्चैव त्रिगुणभावविपर्ययाच्च पुरुषबहुत्वं सिद्धम् ।
units.english: And moreover, because there are different modifications of the three Attributes. Also, by the different modifications of the three Attributes, plurality of the Spirits is proved.

units.sanskrit: यथा सामान्ये जन्मनि एकः सात्त्विकः सुखी । अन्यो राजसो दुःखी ।
units.english: For example, in ordinary life, a Sāttvika person is happy, a Rājasa person is unhappy and a Tāmasa person is under delusion.

units.sanskrit: अन्यस्तामसो मोहवान् । एवं त्रैगुण्यविपर्ययाद्बहुत्वं सिद्धमिति ॥
units.english: And from that contrastfrom that aforesaid viparyāsa, i.e., contrast of the possession of the three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: कैवल्यं माध्यस्थ्यं द्रष्टृत्वमकर्तृभावश्च ॥
units.english: The Spirit is devoid of the Attributes, is discriminative and enjoyer.

units.sanskrit: तस्माच्च विपर्यासात्तस्माच्च यथोक्तत्रैगुण्यविपर्यासाद्विपर्ययान्निर्गुणः पुरुषो विवेकी भोक्तेत्यादिगुणानां पुरुषस्य यो विपर्यास उक्तस्तस्मात् सत्त्वरजस्तमःसु कर्त्तृभूतेषु साक्षित्वं सिद्धं पुरुषस्येति यो ऽयमधिकृतो बहुत्वं प्रति ।
units.english: The contrast is of these qualities in the Spirit, as said before. Therefore, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas being agents active, it follows that the Spirit is endowed with the characteristics of witnessing that Spirit which is the subject of plurality.

units.sanskrit: गुणा एव कर्त्तारः प्रवर्त्तन्ते साक्षी न प्रवत्तते नापि निवर्त्तत एव ।
units.english: Only the Attributes which are agents are active the witness neither acts nor desists from acting.

units.sanskrit: किंचान्यत् कैवल्यं केवलभावः कैवल्यमन्यत्वमित्यर्थः ।
units.english: Moreover, the Spirit is endowed with isolation kaivalya is the property of being isolated or different.

units.sanskrit: त्रिगुणेभ्यः केवलः ।
units.english: That is, isolated or different from that which is possessed of the three Attributes.

units.sanskrit: अन्यन्माध्यस्थ्यं मध्यस्थभावः परिव्राजकवत् मध्यस्थः पुरुषः ।
units.english: Indifference is the property of being indifferent. The Spirit is indifferent like a samnyāsin.

units.sanskrit: यथा कश्चित् परिव्राजको ग्रामीणेषु कर्षणार्थेषु प्रवृत्तेषु केवलो मध्यस्थः पुरुषो ऽप्येवं गुणेषु वर्त्तमानेषु न प्रवर्त्तते ।
units.english: Just as a samnyāsin is indifferent towards the villagers engaged in tilling, so the Spirit also remains indifferent i.e., inactive while the three Attributes are active.

units.sanskrit: तस्माद्द्रष्टृत्वमकर्त्तृभावाश्च यस्मान्मध्यस्थस्तस्माद्द्रष्टा तस्मादकर्त्ता पुरुषस्तेषां कर्मणामिति सत्त्वरजस्तमांसि त्रयो गुणाः कर्मकर्त्तृभावेन प्रवर्त्तन्ते न पुरुष एवं पुरुषस्यास्तित्वं च सिद्धम् ।
units.english: Therefore, the Spirit is endowed with perception and inactivity. Because the Spirit is indifferent, therefore, it is the perceiver and notagent of those actions. The Attributes, Sattva, Rajas and Tamas function as agents and action, and not the Spirit. Thus also the existence of the Spirit is proved.

units.sanskrit: यस्मात्कर्त्ता पुरुषस्तत्कथमध्यवसायं करोति धर्मं करिष्याम्यधर्मं न करिष्यामीत्यतः कर्त्ता भवति न च कर्त्ता पुरुष एवमुभयात्र दोषः स्यादिति ॥
units.english: Objection“If the Spirit is a nonagent, then how does it exercise volition in the shape of,‘I shall practise virtue, I will not practise vice’.

units.sanskrit: अत उच्यते ।
units.english: Therefore, it is an agent.

units.sanskrit: गुणकर्तृत्वे ऽपि तथा कर्तेव भवत्युदासीनः ॥
units.english: And although the activity belongs to the Attributes, yet the indifferent Spirit seems as if it were an agent.
